front.title: Aether: An Adaptive Sub-IP Network Coding Transport Protocol for Highly Lossy Wireless Environments

abstract.t: This document specifies Aether, a sovereign sub-IP and UDP-encapsulated transport protocol engineered for operating environments characterized by extreme non-congestive physical-layer packet loss (10% to 30%), severe bufferbloat, and asymmetric cellular connectivity. Aether unifies Fulcrum Network Coding (concatenated GF(2) outer expansion and sliding-window GF(2^8) inner random linear coding) with an Extended Kalman Filter (EKF) delay-gradient congestion controller, zero-copy kernel bypass, and subspace homomorphic vector MAC authentication to eliminate transport collapses caused by non-congestive RF fading.

section.title: Introduction
section.t: Contemporary transport protocols, including TCP Cubic (RFC 8312), TCP BBR, and standard QUIC (RFC 9000), interpret physical packet losses or sharp latency variations as primary indicators of intermediate queue saturation (congestion). In sub-Saharan African mobile deployments—specifically 4G LTE and 5G non-standalone infrastructure in Nigeria—uplinks experience severe non-congestive packet drops resulting from tropical atmospheric attenuation, Rayleigh multipath fading, and carrier-grade NAT timeouts.

Aether separates loss recovery from congestion notification by integrating rateless Fulcrum Network Coding directly into the transport framing layer, allowing receivers to reconstruct dropped symbols on the fly without waiting for Round-Trip Time (RTT) stall-inducing retransmission requests.

section.title: Terminology and Notation
section.t: The key words "MUST", "MUST NOT", "REQUIRED", "SHALL", "SHALL NOT", "SHOULD", "SHOULD NOT", "RECOMMENDED", "NOT RECOMMENDED", "MAY", and "OPTIONAL" in this document are to be interpreted as described in BCP 14 [RFC2119] [RFC8174].

list.t: Symbol: An atomic chunk of transmission payload of fixed size S bytes.
Generation / Window (K): The block size of source symbols encoded together.
GF(2^8): Galois Field of size 256 defined by irreducible polynomial P(x) = x^8 + x^4 + x^3 + x + 1 (0x11D).
Degrees of Freedom (DoF): Number of linearly independent coded packets accumulated by the receiver.

section.title: Fulcrum Network Coding Layer
section.t: Aether utilizes a two-tier concatenated coding structure:
1. Outer Binary Expansion: K source packets are expanded into K + r intermediate symbols via a sparse generator matrix over GF(2), executed using simple bitwise XOR operations.
2. Inner Random Linear Coding: Intermediate symbols are combined over GF(2^8) to synthesize rateless repair packets.

This design allows low-power receivers to decode systematically in O(1) complexity under benign channel conditions, falling back to full Gaussian-Jordan elimination only when channel degradation demands it.

section.title: Delay-Gradient EKF Congestion Arbiter
section.t: Instead of cutting transmission windows upon packet loss, Aether executes an Extended Kalman Filter tracking the one-way queuing delay gradient d(Delta)/dt. When packet loss occurs while the delay gradient is less than or equal to zero, the loss is attributed to physical wireless degradation; pacing rates are preserved and coding redundancy is proactively increased.

section.title: Packet Format
section.t: Aether packets feature a compact, 16-byte fixed-size little-endian header preceding the symbol payload:

Header fields:
Sequential identifier of the active coding window. Index of the symbol within the window (0..K-1 for systematic, >=K for repair). Source symbol count K for this generation. Deterministic PRNG seed used to generate GF(2^8) linear coefficients. Bitflags for FIN, PROBE, CELL_TELEMETRY, and PATH_ID. CRC-16-CCITT checksum over header and payload. Subspace homomorphic vector MAC authentication tag.

section.title: Security Considerations
section.t: Linear network coding systems are vulnerable to Byzantine pollution attacks, wherein an adversary injects bogus linear combinations that corrupt the entire decoding matrix during Gaussian-Jordan elimination. Aether enforces subspace homomorphic vector MACs derived from an X25519 shared secret established at session initiation. Incoming packets failing subspace verification are discarded prior to matrix ingestion.

section.title: IANA Considerations
section.t: This document requests IANA to assign UDP port 4242 to the Aether Transport Protocol.
